title: Weighted Bid Evaluation Rubric: Scoring Free First Month & Deep-Clean Credit Proposals
seoTitle: Weighted Evaluation Rubric: Scoring Free First Month & Deep Clean Bids
metaDescription: Apply a weighted evaluation rubric when negotiating a free first month or deep-clean credit ($0.07–$0.15/sq ft). Score bids in our quote comparator.
excerpt: When three janitorial bidders pitch different promotional incentives—one offering a free first month, another offering a free initial deep clean, and a third quoting a straight net rate—how do you compare them apples-to-apples? Use this 100-point weighted evaluation rubric to normalize net first-year cost and protect nightly labor hours.
quickAnswer: A reliable weighted evaluation rubric for negotiating a free first month or deep clean credit assigns 30 points to True Net Annualized Cost & Base Rate Integrity ($0.07 to $0.15/sq ft per visit for 2,500–24,999 sq ft suites), 25 points to Guaranteed Nightly Labor Hours ($35 to $65/hr at 3,500 sq ft/hr ISSA production), 20 points to Verifiable Deep-Clean & Quarterly Floor Scope ($0.03 to $0.06/sq ft/mo value), 15 points to Fair Clawback & Exit Terms (pro-rata 180-day burn-off), and 10 points to Dispenser & Consumable Controls. Reject any bid scoring under 75/100.

blocks.text: How to Normalize Competing Promotional Concessions Across Janitorial Bids

During a competitive janitorial RFP, commercial cleaning contractors rarely structure their pricing proposals identically. Vendor A might quote $3,100 per month with no promotional discounts; Vendor B might quote $3,450 per month with a 'Free First Month'; and Vendor C might quote $3,250 per month with a 'Complimentary Initial Restorative Deep Clean and Free Touchless Dispenser Upgrade.' Without a financial normalization formula and an objective scoring matrix, procurement teams frequently fall for headline giveaways that actually cost more over a 12-to-24-month cycle.

Deploying a structured weighted evaluation rubric negotiating free first month or deep clean credit proposals forces every bid onto a level playing field. It separates genuine capital concessions from pre-discount price padding and verifies that no bidder is cannibalizing nightly custodian hours to fund their sales promotion.

blocks.title: The Net Effective Monthly Cost (NEMC) Normalization Formula
blocks.text: Before assigning rubric points, calculate each bidder's Net Effective Monthly Cost over Year 1: take (Base Monthly Fee x 12) + (Annualized Add-Ons for Breakroom, Glass, and Quarterly Floor Care) - (Verified Dollar Value of Free Month or Initial Deep-Clean Credit), then divide by 12. Next, verify that the vendor's Year-2 renewal rate—after one-time credits expire—remains within 2026 national benchmarks ($0.09–$0.15/sq ft/visit for 2,500–9,999 sq ft; $0.07–$0.12/sq ft/visit for 10,000–24,999 sq ft).
100-Point Weighted Evaluation Rubric for Discounted & Credited Janitorial Proposals

Score each finalist from 1 to 5 across the five procurement dimensions below, then multiply by the category weight to calculate a 100-point composite score. Require a minimum score of 78/100 for contract award.

blocks.caption: 100-Point Weighted Evaluation Rubric for Free First Month & Deep-Clean Credit Proposals
rows: 1. Base Rate Integrity & Net Year-1/Year-2 Cost
30 pts (Weight x 6)
Inflates base rate >12% above benchmark to offset free month; expensive Year-2 jump
Base rate sits within size-tier benchmark; offers 50% off Month 1 or initial clean
Competitive un-padded base rate ($0.07–$0.15/sq ft) + full month credit (Month 6/12) or deep clean
2. Guaranteed Nightly Man-Hours & Wage Realism
25 pts (Weight x 5)
Refuses to disclose nightly labor hours; implies <$30/hr or >4,800 sq ft/hr speed
States estimated daily shift hours aligned with $35–$65/hr standard billing range
Contractually guarantees nightly & monthly man-hours (3,500 sq ft/hr ISSA benchmark) via GPS clock-in
3. Deep-Clean & Quarterly Floor Scope Rigor
20 pts (Weight x 4)
Vague 'free deep clean' promise with zero machine hours or extraction specs
Includes initial carpet extraction or VCT scrub ($0.15–$0.25/sq ft one-time value)
Itemizes specialty tech hours ($55–$95/hr) for initial extraction/grout scrub + $0.03–$0.06/sq ft/mo quarterly plan
4. Clawback Fairness & Contract Exit Flexibility
15 pts (Weight x 3)
Requires 24–36 month lock-in; demands 100% credit payback even if fired for cause
12-month agreement with 30-day notice; pro-rata clawback over 12 months
30-day termination for convenience; pro-rata clawback expires after 180 days; $0 payback if terminated for cause
5. Dispenser Hardware Upgrade & Consumable Cap
10 pts (Weight x 2)
Excludes consumables from credit and inflates paper/soap above $0.028/sq ft/visit
Transparent per-case consumable pricing ($0.012–$0.025/sq ft/visit) with no markup spikes
Provides free touchless/coreless dispenser hardware upgrade + locked per-case consumable ceiling

blocks.text: Worked Comparison Example: Scoring Three Competing 12,000 Sq Ft Bids

To see how this weighted evaluation rubric exposes hidden price padding, consider a 12,000 Usable Square Foot (USF) corporate office requesting 5x/week nightly service (21.65 visits per month based on 4.33 weeks/month and a 0.90x daily frequency multiplier) with mixed carpet and hard flooring (1.05x surface multiplier):

items: Bidder A ('Free First Month' Pitch — Scores 62/100): Quotes $0.145/sq ft per visit ($3,767/month) and waives Month 1 ($3,767 credit). Year-1 net spend is $41,437 ($3,453/month effective), but Year-2 spend jumps to $45,204. Furthermore, Bidder A refuses to guarantee nightly labor hours and imposes a 24-month lock-in with a 100% clawback.

Bidder B ('Straight Lowball' Pitch — Scores 68/100): Quotes $0.072/sq ft per visit ($1,870/month) with zero concessions. However, auditing Criterion 2 reveals Bidder B allocates only 1.8 nightly labor hours for 12,000 sq ft (an impossible 6,667 sq ft/hour pace—nearly double the ISSA 3,500 sq ft/hour limit) and excludes breakroom detailing ($12–$25/visit) and interior glass ($15–$35/visit).

Bidder C ('Initial Deep-Clean + Earned Month-6/12 Credit' — Scores 92/100): Quotes an accurate $0.095/sq ft per visit ($2,980/month inclusive of breakroom and interior glass add-ons), guarantees 3.5 nightly labor hours (75.78 hours/month at $39.32/hour), provides a complimentary 16-hour weekend restorative deep clean on Day 1 ($1,280 value at $80/hr specialty rate), and applies a 50% credit in Month 6 and Month 12 ($2,980 total credit). Year-1 net effective cost is $2,625/month ($31,500 total) with full labor transparency and a 180-day pro-rata convenience-only clawback.

blocks.text: Scoring Criterion 5: Hardware Concessions That Deliver Recurring Savings (10 Points)

When evaluating Criterion 5, award top marks (4 to 5 raw points, or 8 to 10 weighted points) to vendors who supplement their proposal with commercial dispenser upgrades that permanently lower your ongoing consumable run rate ($0.012 to $0.025 per sq ft per visit) and reduce nightly custodian refill time:

items: Touch-Free Reception & Corridor Sanitizer Stations: Vendors who supply and install the GOJO PURELL ES8 Touch-Free Hand Sanitizer Dispenser (1200 mL cartridge capacity, Energy-on-the-Refill battery integration that eliminates dead-dispenser maintenance calls, ADA-compliant depth profile, and At-a-Glance refill windows) add tangible amenity value to reception desks and conference hubs.

High-Capacity Coreless Restroom Tissue Fixtures: Upgrading standard two-roll cored holders to the Scott Pro High-Capacity Coreless Standard Roll Dispenser (Kimberly-Clark, holding 4 coreless standard rolls in an ADA-compliant housing with keyed or keyless locking) cuts stub-roll paper waste by up to 15% and slashes custodian restocking minutes.

High-Yield Touchless Counter & Wall Foam Soap Dispensers: Standardizing restrooms and breakroom sinks on the Rubbermaid Commercial AutoFoam 1100 mL Touchless Soap Dispenser (delivering up to 2,750 metered foam handwashes per 1100 mL refill pouch with a 3-year battery life and ADA compliance) prevents messy liquid soap drips and lowers annual soap pouch consumption.

blocks.title: How to Score Net-10 ACH Prompt-Pay Discounts in Criterion 1
blocks.text: Ask every bidder during the RFP Q&A round: 'What percentage discount off base monthly billing will you grant if we enroll in Net-10 ACH automatic payment?' Award an extra raw point in Criterion 1 to vendors offering a 3% to 4% prompt-pay discount, which stacks cleanly on top of an initial deep-clean credit without reducing custodian wages.
4-Step Verification Workflow Before Awarding the Contract
Before finalizing your rubric scores and issuing an award letter, complete these four verification steps:

items.name: Step 1: Audit All Bids Across a 24-Month Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) Horizon
items.text: Model both Year-1 spend (including one-time free months or initial deep-clean credits) and Year-2 spend (including any CPI escalation cap, ideally capped at 3.0% to 3.5%). A vendor with a slightly smaller Year-1 promo credit often wins on 24-month TCO if their base square-foot rate is 8% cleaner.

items.name: Step 2: Verify Nightly Man-Hours Against Surface & Frequency Multipliers
items.text: Check that each finalist applied the correct frequency multiplier (1.08x for 1x/week at 4.33 visits/mo; 1.00x for 2x/week at 8.66 visits/mo; 0.95x for 3x/week at 13.0 visits/mo; 0.90x for 5x/week at 21.65 visits/mo) and flooring multiplier (1.00x carpet, 1.04x VCT/LVT, 1.08x hardwood, 1.12x ceramic tile & grout).

items.name: Step 3: Require a Separate Onboarding Deep-Clean Sign-Off Checklist
items.text: If scoring a proposal that includes a complimentary initial deep clean, attach an Onboarding Acceptance Checklist requiring the facility manager's signature after inspecting carpet extraction, grout scrubbing, and high dusting before the promotional credit is deemed fulfilled.

items.name: Step 4: Confirm COI, OSHA HazCom, and Clawback Redlines in Final Contract Draft
items.text: Verify the vendor's Certificate of Insurance ($1M/$2M General Liability + statutory Workers' Comp), on-site OSHA Safety Data Sheet (SDS) binder protocol, and 180-day convenience-only pro-rata clawback wording prior to execution.

faqs.q: Should a 'Free First Month' score higher than a 'Complimentary Initial Deep Clean' of equal dollar value?
faqs.a: No—when both concessions carry the same dollar value (e.g., $2,500), an Initial Restorative Deep Clean or an Earned Month-6/Month-12 Credit should score 1 to 2 raw points higher in Criterion 3 and Criterion 4. An initial deep clean physically restores neglected carpets, grout, and VCT on Weekend 1 so nightly maintenance succeeds, whereas a Month-1 invoice waiver deprives the contractor of startup cash flow when onboarding costs are highest.

faqs.q: How do we score a vendor that offers a free quarterly floor-care program instead of a free first month?
faqs.a: Calculate the annualized dollar value of the quarterly deep floor care program using the national benchmark of $0.03 to $0.06 per sq ft per month (for a 10,000 sq ft office, that equals $300 to $600/month or $3,600 to $7,200/year in hot-water carpet extraction and VCT scrub-and-recoat value). Frequently, a waived or 50%-discounted quarterly floor program is worth 1.2x to 1.8x more over 12 months than a single free month of base cleaning.

faqs.q: What is the minimum acceptable score on Criterion 2 (Guaranteed Nightly Labor Hours)?
faqs.a: Require at least a 3 out of 5 (15 out of 25 weighted points) on Criterion 2 as a mandatory threshold. Any bidder scoring a 1 out of 5—by hiding their nightly labor hours or proposing an implied hourly rate below $35/hour or a cleaning speed faster than 4,500 sq ft/hour for a standard office—will inevitably cut corners to pay for their promotional discount.

faqs.q: How do we verify that dispenser hardware offered as a free contract concession doesn't lock us into overpriced refills?
faqs.a: Before awarding points in Criterion 5 for free dispenser installations, require the vendor to list the exact replacement refill part numbers and lock in a per-case price ceiling for the 12-month term. Choosing widespread commercial systems like Scott Pro coreless bath tissue, Rubbermaid AutoFoam 1100 mL refills, or GOJO PURELL ES8 cartridges ensures you can benchmark refill case prices across multiple national janitorial distributors.
